statement: For every connected acyclic t:X→W and arbitrary possibly empty or disconnected Y, t*:Map(W,Y)→Map(X,Y) is a weak equivalence onto precisely the components killing ker π₁t.

statement: A λ-cell connected CW complex has a λ-cell acyclic aspherical resolution; this proves the remembered size premise and completes the audit of R2 Proof 1.
manuscript_pages_settled: V ms. 44–46, as input to the invariant-presheaf results in Part B
notes: Original Kan–Thurston attribution is not used; every lifting, amalgam, Mayer–Vietoris, small-image and limit step is checked.

statement: A π₁-surjective based map BH→W extends through a group embedding H↪G and an acyclic BG→W, with BH retained as a CW subcomplex and the infinite cardinal bound retained.
manuscript_pages_settled: V ms. 44–46, as input to the invariant-presheaf results in Part B
notes: Relative cells have dimension at least two; actual compatible maps, not just homotopy classes, are preserved.

statement: R2 can be realized with nonabelian simple kernel P and |P|=|G|=λ, for every infinite λ>μ bounding a CW model of W.
manuscript_pages_settled: V ms. 44–46, as input to the invariant-presheaf results in Part B

statement: Every acyclic BG→W induces a deck-equivariant acyclic BP→W̃, hence H_*(P;Z)≅H_*(W̃;Z) as Z[π₁W]-modules; these exact values are realizable with P simple.
manuscript_pages_settled: V ms. 44–46, as input to the invariant-presheaf results in Part B
notes: This is the complete restriction on prescribing kernel homology for fixed W; the same map preserves cohomology and cup products.

statement: R2 is functorial for injective simplicial maps, and an explicit replacement is functorial for all simplicial maps, retaining acyclicity and the no-small-image bound.
manuscript_pages_settled: V ms. 44–46, as input to the invariant-presheaf results in Part B
notes: The arbitrary-map replacement retains degenerate simplices in Δ_inj/S, then uses the nerve face poset; all comparisons and cardinal bounds are proved.

statement: The original simple-cone models cannot extend unchanged to all simplicial maps; an acyclic-resolution functor cannot have simple kernel on every simply connected input.
manuscript_pages_settled: V ms. 44–46, as input to the invariant-presheaf results in Part B
notes: Explicit retractions Δ²↪Δ³ and S²↪S²∨S² force impossible homology isomorphisms; finite chain computations are program checked.

statement: Every finite-dimensional connected CW W has a same-dimensional acyclic BG→W satisfying R2 for every finite μ; finite/countable/cardinal model bounds are retained.
manuscript_pages_settled: V ms. 44–46, as input to the invariant-presheaf results in Part B
notes: Higman no-finite-image property and normal generation of BDH cone groups are checked explicitly; infinite CW union dimension is controlled by actual compatible models.

statement: Nontrivial P requires μ<|G|. For countable nonaspherical finite-dimensional W and countable same-dimensional BG, existence holds exactly for finite μ. Dimension alone does not bound μ for all W.
manuscript_pages_settled: V ms. 44–46, as input to the invariant-presheaf results in Part B
notes: Identity G→G gives the necessary bound; graph identities give the stated absence of a dimension-only bound.

statement: Every connected non-1-type Y admits an essential map BG→Y, with G nonabelian simple of cardinality max(ℵ₀, μ⁺), and every homomorphism from G to a group of cardinality at most μ trivial.
manuscript_pages_settled: CATHOT essential group tests used in strict category obstruction
notes: Choose an essential sphere in the universal cover; precomposition along A.6 is injective by the full mapping-space equivalence A.2. A nullhomotopy after projection lifts and ends in a discrete fibre, hence is constant.

statement: For every infinite λ, there is an acyclic map BS_λ→∨_λ S² with S_λ nonabelian simple of size λ and BS_λ two-dimensional; it satisfies R2 for all μ<λ. Therefore dimension alone bounds no μ, even for nonaspherical targets.
manuscript_pages_settled: A3(iii): refutes the dimension-only bound, including nonaspherical targets
notes: Use only the simple-envelope HNN construction on F_λ. The h=1 relations supply λ independent cellular H₂ classes, and no three-cells are present. A split cellular-chain retraction gives the actual acyclic map to the wedge of λ two-spheres. This does not settle infinite μ for a fixed target such as S².
